diffs.diff: header pin 2: part says GND, datasheet reading says 3Vo
diffs.evidence: Adafruit MAX31865 board file (Adafruit MAX31865.brd): header JP1 (1X08_ROUND_70 at x=12.7) pad 2 (x=3.81+2.54=6.35) is on signal GND (with regulator U3 pad 2), and the silkscreen text 'GND' sits at x=6.477 above it. Order on the silkscreen left to right: VIN(3.81) GND(6.477) 3V3(8.89) CLK(11.557) SDO(13.97) SDI(16.51) CS(19.05) RDY(21.844). The Learn page lists 'Vin, 3Vo, GND' as a functional description, not the physical pin order.

diffs.diff: header pin 3: part says 3V3, datasheet reading says GND
diffs.evidence: Adafruit MAX31865.brd: JP1 pad 3 (x=8.89) is on signal VDD together with regulator U3 pad 5 (its 3.3 V output); silkscreen text '3V3' at x=8.89. Learn page: '3Vo - this is the 3.3V output from the voltage regulator, you can grab up to 100mA'. The part models it as the regulator output (nc, not a supply input), which matches.

diffs.diff: RTD resistance (ohm), 15-bit ratio x 430 ohm Rref / 32768: datasheet reading gives 0.01312256 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: MAX31865 datasheet: 'RRTD = (ADC Code x RREF)/2^15', 'ADC Code = 15-bit ADC results from RTD Data registers'. The part already models this: sim.spiReplies match '01' has a 15-bit 'value' control with scale 0.01312255859375 (= 430/32768) followed by a 1-bit fault flag, and the driver computes read_raw() * rref / 32768 with rref=430. The gate's conversion scan reads only sim.measure/measures/responses, not spiReplies, so it reports 'none'.
